newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares tumble as FIIs turn sellers.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares tumble as FIIs turn sellers.

text.p: Share prices on the Delhi Stock Exchange closed sharply lower on Thursday as foreign institutional investors (FIIs) unloaded their stocks at higher levels, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index closed 14.07 points lower at 647.95.

Traders said the market failed to sustain high levels as investors, who had built huge positions buoyed by Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's remarks that the minimum alternate tax (MAT) could be reviewed, offloaded at higher price levels.
"Today's activity was mostly of speculative nature as buyers and sellers were equally active throughout the session," said Vijay Aggarwal of brokers Mass Financial Services.
Deve Gowda said on Tuesday that he would consider a request by industry to remove the recently-introduced MAT on companies when next year's budget is prepared.
Cement maker ACC, after remaining volatile throughout the session, finally closed 36.05 rupees lower at 1,000, brokers said.
Reliance Industries fell 7 rupees to 187.40 on profit-taking.
TISCO closed 5.10 rupees lower at 154.40 on heavy FII selling coupled with profit-taking by speculators.
State Bank of India dropped 6.80 rupees to 208.90.
